ratings_why.fun: Every turn is a placement puzzle (fill the ground or leave it bare), and heirs waking mid-fight give the board drama, though the rule load slows the first few games.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: no tribe today punishes its own members for standing together; 'a Knight next to a Knight goes blank' turns the zigzag into one exact lek shape and makes the empty ground the tribe's other half.

verdict_why: Pennon-Bearer's 'or' reads as a choice; one rewording fixes it, and the Squire text can be shortened while at it.

points.text: Pennon-Bearer's 'or' reads as a choice the player makes. Say: 'give your other Knights +1/+1 permanently; those next to one of this unit's Gallery units get +2/+2 instead.'
Squire can be one line in the same shape as Deaf: 'Squire: never puts another Knight off Station.' That says the one-way blank and the two-Squires case without three sentences.
Five terms plus three rule-bending cards is heavy. Fold Deaf into Sir Hartmut's own text ('The Lek ignores this') so one keyword goes.
Add to the Takes Station reminder: 'not if it starts the fight on Station'. Players will otherwise expect a lone Rupprecht or Konrad to fire every fight.

standouts.why: Dame Reisig judges, crowns the biggest Knight and walks out: the hen's whole story in one Start of Combat line.
Sir Einsiedel reads at a glance ('alone, double') and pays off the bare-ground plan; his combo with Reisig is easy to discover.
Sir Brennbart, the mad cock who blasts his own side, is honest text with clear flavour, and turns the Gallery into a battery.

weakest.why: Sprucehold Envoy is pure rule edit with nothing of its own to do; hard to picture on the board and has little woodland flavour.
Sir Hartmut is a plain attack-twice body; his deafness lives in a keyword printed on one card.
Edge-Strutter is generic; at F1 or F4 only one slot can be beside it, so the text barely moves.

flags.note: 'or' can be read as a choice between the two buffs.
Four Heather Hens around a B2 Herald of the Old Lek give 8 gold a turn, 16 golden.
One kill on Grand Master Ottokar blanks the whole crowd; it needs clear on-screen feedback when Station drops.
